title: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, and Evidence Workflows - Consolidated Guidance
author: Asha Patel
summary: Authoritative, consolidated operational guidance for RBAC & authentication, audit logging and retention, data residency and deletion, secure SDLC gates, security incident response, automated compliance evidence generation, and the risk & exceptions process.
body:
Purpose and scope:

This document centralizes Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls and operational workflows for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging and retention, data residency and retention, secure SDLC gates integrated into CI/CD, security-focused incident response procedures, automated compliance evidence workflows, and the risk & exceptions process. It applies across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments unless a customer contract imposes stricter controls.

1) RBAC & Authentication:
- Principle: least privilege by default; prefer role-based grants and avoid ad-hoc individual permissions.
- Supported IdPs: Okta (primary), Google Workspace (secondary), SCIM provisioning for service accounts.
- Canonical roles and owners: org-admin (Platform), infra-engineer (Eng Infra), runtime-operator (Eng Serving Runtime), sec-audit (Security), app-developer (Product/Eng), support-analyst (Customer Success).
- MFA: required (TOTP or hardware security key) for all human accounts with production access.
- Service accounts: interactive use prohibited; long-lived credentials require ticketed justification, are stored in Vault/KMS, and rotate every 90 days.
- Access request lifecycle: submit via Jira template -> manager + resource owner approval -> TTL assigned (max 30 days for elevated roles unless approved) -> automated expiry/JIT issuance where supported.
- Auditing: every IAM change, policy edit, and SCIM event logged and included in weekly membership reports for org-admin and sec-audit.

2) Audit Logging:
- Objective: provide detectability, traceability, and preserved forensic artifacts for investigations and audits.
- Minimum sources collected: IdP auth events (Okta), control-plane API actions, runtime lifecycle events, Kubernetes/VM audit logs, cloud console events, and customer data access logs where applicable.
- Aggregation pipeline: events -> Kafka ingest -> enrichment -> Datadog (metrics/alerts) + Splunk (hot search) + S3 (warm storage) -> Glacier/cold archive as needed.
- Integrity controls: ingestion batches checksummed and signed; daily checksum verification job that opens a security ticket on mismatch.
- SLOs/thresholds: 99.99% of events ingested within 5 minutes; page oncall if no events from any prod control-plane service for >3 minutes.
- Retention (audit logs): default hot: 1 year (Splunk/Datadog), warm S3: 3 years, cold archive: 7 years for regulatory customers. Sensitive events (auth failures, privilege elevations) hot retention: 2 years.
- Log access: controlled via sec-audit role and short-lived grants; ad-hoc access requires approval and is logged in access audit.

3) Data Residency & Retention:
- Principle: honor customer-selected region at provisioning; separate telemetry from customer PII.
- Controls: region tagging for buckets/DBs/snapshots; cross-region replication disabled by default for customer data unless contractually permitted.
- Retention examples: runtime non-PII logs: 90 days hot; customer model artifacts default: 180 days (customer-configurable); compliance artifacts/evidence: 7 years.
- Customer data erasure workflow: validate requester identity -> quarantine resources and snapshot state -> run deterministic deletion job (CLI documented) -> produce deletion certificate -> update data inventory and evidence store.

4) Secure SDLC (CI/CD controls):
- Mandatory gates: threat modeling for services handling customer data or inference at scale; 2 approver code review (one cross-team reviewer for sensitive services); CI scans include SAST, SCA, license checks, secret scanning, and container image vulnerability scanning.
- Pre-deploy tests: integration tests exercising auth, authorization, and residency behaviors in staging.
- Secrets policy: no secrets in repos; CI injects secrets from Vault and developers use ephemeral tokens locally.
- PR release checklist (attached to PR): threat model updated (Y/N), SAST: zero critical/high or documented mitigations, dependency scan: no critical CVEs or mitigations documented, secrets check: pass, perf/load smoke: pass, owner sign-offs obtained.
- Shift-left & training: quarterly security training for engineers, monthly vulnerability digests, and a triage board for dependency fixes.

5) Incident Response  Security Procedures:
- Objectives: rapid containment, evidence preservation, stakeholder engagement, remediation, and timely customer/regulator notification where required.
- Lifecycle: Detection & Triage -> Classification -> Containment -> Forensics -> Remediation -> Recovery -> Post-incident review and evidence package generation.
- Example privilege-escalation runbook excerpt: revoke affected user's sessions via control-plane API, rotate service account keys (vault rotate), snapshot logs and S3 objects for the incident, and isolate affected hosts.
- Communication & escalation: pager: oncall-security (primary), oncall-platform (secondary); exec notification chain: VP Security -> CTO -> CEO on confirmed customer impact or material data exposure; customer notification per contractual/legal thresholds.
- Evidence preservation: immutable copies of logs and snapshots placed in encrypted evidence bucket with restricted access; every retrieval is audited and logged in the incident ticket.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows:
- Goal: enable repeatable, auditable evidence packages for SOC2, ISO27001, and legal discovery with minimal manual effort.
- Evidence orchestrator: internal service that produces time-bound packages containing configuration snapshots, RBAC membership lists, audit log slices, training records, and SDLC artifacts mapped to controls.
- Manifest contents: each package includes a manifest (id, time_range, contents list, owner, digest/signature) signed by Security; manifest included as plain text in the package.
- Storage and retention: packages stored encrypted in compliance S3 with 7-year retention by default; access strictly limited and audited.
- Review cadence: quarterly internal compliance reviews to validate evidence generation and integrity.

7) Risk & Exceptions:
- Purpose: document temporary, approved deviations from standard controls where compensating controls mitigate residual risk to acceptable levels.
- Workflow: submit Jira Risk Exception (scope, justification, compensating controls, mitigation plan, TTL) -> Security assigns risk rating (Low/Medium/High) -> Approvals: Security Manager for Low; Security Leadership + CTO for Medium/High; Legal as required -> define enhanced monitoring/alerts for exception lifespan -> exception auto-expires at TTL and requires re-approval for renewal.
- Record keeping & metrics: risk register maintained in Security wiki (CSV exportable); monthly metrics tracked: active exceptions, average approval time, and renewals.

8) Operational owners & runbooks:
- Primary contacts: security@redwood-inference.internal, infra-ops@redwood-inference.internal, runtime-ops@redwood-inference.internal, cs-data-ops@redwood-inference.internal.
- Referenced runbooks: RBAC change runbook, log ingestion & pipeline runbook, incident-response playbook (see related_pages).
